components.gap: Hypotheses element not plainly supplied: the statement reads 'positive black weight b, red weight r and same-color reinforcement c>0', which qualifies b and c but leaves the red weight r unqualified. The conclusion that the c_n are 'precisely the moments of beta(b/c,r/c)' requires r>0 (the handbook's beta law, def:p15-beta-integral, is defined only for both parameters positive, and the cited exchangeability theorem thm:p15-polya-word-law assumes r>0); at r=0 the formula gives c_n=1, the moments of delta_1, and no beta law exists. Positivity of r is therefore an unstated assumption under the plain reading. All other elements (product and gamma forms of c_n, empty product, beta moments, Hausdorff identification, word and count probabilities, agreement with the direct urn law) are present at the cited lines.

defect_observations.note: Write 'positive black and red weights b, r' (or add r>0) so the beta(b/c,r/c) identification and the cited thm:p15-polya-word-law hypotheses are plainly met.

Exchangeability of the urn draws is justified by 'the same numerator-permutation argument as in the direct urn proof'; thm:p15-polya-word-law already states exchangeability for this urn after renaming and could be cited by label instead.

The Poisson and gamma cases take real n->infinity, but thm:p15-feller-concentration is stated for positive integers n. The per-law estimate displayed at annex lines 11-14 covers real n; a one-line remark (or a real-index statement of the lemma) would make the application literal.
The binomial reciprocity identity (Feller (1.10)) is derived by substitution but never displayed; later proofs (annex 97, 193) invoke it by name only.

Uniqueness of lambda is transferred from the uniqueness of the directing law; the step that word probabilities fix all finite-coordinate mixture probabilities (finite sums over words) is left implicit, and the cited frequency theorem is stated for the chosen class C, which contains the singletons only if C is chosen as the power set of the finite alphabet.
The harmonic-series comparison needs C^{1/(2n)} bounded (C>=m_0=1, so C^{1/(2n)}<=C^{1/2}); this is not stated.

'the already proved Bernoulli central limit theorem' (thm:p15-stirling-general-binomial) and, at annex line 47, 'the already proved gamma formulas' (thm:p15-gamma-normalization) are referenced without labels; both exist and are proved on the route.
Delta_h^2 u(0)=-2 for u=x-x^2 is asserted as 'a direct calculation' without the one-line substitution.
